speaker: Doctor
text: To better understand your symptoms, can you tell me when these issues with double vision, climbing stairs, and arm weakness began? Have you noticed any difficulty swallowing or slurred speech as well?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That pattern of worsening with activity and improving with rest is very telling. Have you noticed any specific weakness in your eyelids or throat, such as drooping or choking when you eat? Also, do you have a history of thyroid disease or myasthenia gravis?

REQUEST TEST: Anticholinesterase challenge test, Thyroid_function_panel

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs.

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had trouble swallowing or slurred speech. I also have not noticed breathing difficulty, and the symptoms started gradually about a month ago.

speaker: Patient
text: The weakness is clearly worse with exertion and better after rest. I have not noticed muscle wasting or weight loss. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Tuberculosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis. The patient's history of fluctuating weakness worsening with activity and improving with rest, combined with double vision (ophthalmoplegia), is classic for this condition. The previous suggestion of tuberculosis does not align with the specific symptom pattern of fatigue-induced weakness.
